arxiv-1905-04359.title: The Swift UVOT Stars Survey. III. Photometry and Color-Magnitude Diagrams of 103 Galactic Open Clusters
arxiv-1905-04359.creator: Michael H. Siegel, Samuel J. LaPorte, Blair L. Porterfield, Lea M. Z. Hagen, Caryl A. Gronwall
arxiv-1905-04359.description: Abstract As part of the Swift/UVOT Stars Survey, we present near-ultraviolet (3000-1700 Å) point-source photometry for 103 Galactic open clusters. These data, taken over the span of the mission, provide a unique and unprecedented set of near-ultraviolet point-source photometry on simple stellar populations.

arxiv-2111-00458.title: Spherical curves whose curvature depends on distance to a great circle Dedicated to Professor Óscar Garay, in memoriam
arxiv-2111-00458.creator: Ildefonso Castro, Ildefonso Castro-Infantes, Jesús Castro-Infantes
arxiv-2111-00458.description: Abstract . Motivated by a problem posed by David A. Singer in 1999 and by the elastic spherical curves, we study the spherical curves whose curvature is expressed in terms of the distance to a great circle (or from a point).

arxiv-2210-17409.title: Deep Model Reassembly
arxiv-2210-17409.creator: Xingyi Yang, Daquan Zhou, Songhua Liu, Jingwen Ye, Xinchao Wang
arxiv-2210-17409.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xingyi Yang, Daquan Zhou, Songhua Liu, Jingwen Ye, Xinchao Wang. In this paper, we explore a novel knowledge-transfer task, termed as Deep Model Reassembly ( DeRy ), for general-purpose model reuse. Given a collection of heterogeneous models pre-trained from distinct sources and with diverse architectures, the goal of DeRy , as its name implies, is to first dissect each model into distinctive building blocks, and then selectively reassemble the derived blocks to produce customized networks under both the hardware resource and performance constraints.

arxiv-2409-20087.title: Inferring Thunderstorm Occurrence from Vertical Profiles of Convection-Permitting Simulations: Physical Insights from a Physical Deep Learning Model
arxiv-2409-20087.description: Abstract Thunderstorms have significant social and economic impacts due to heavy precipitation, hail, lightning, and strong winds, necessitating reliable forecasts. Thunderstorm forecasts based on numerical weather prediction (NWP) often rely on single-level surrogate predictors, like convective available potential energy and convective inhibition, derived from vertical profiles of three-dimensional atmospheric variables.

arxiv-2411-15044.title: Untangling Magellanic Streams
arxiv-2411-15044.creator: Dennis Zaritsky 1, Vedant Chandra 2, Charlie Conroy 2, Ana Bonaca 3, Phillip A. Cargile 2, Rohan P. Naidu 4,5
arxiv-2411-15044.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Dennis Zaritsky 1, Vedant Chandra 2, Charlie Conroy 2, Ana Bonaca 3, Phillip A. Cargile 2, Rohan P. Naidu 4,5. The Magellanic Stream (MS) has long been known to contain multiple H I strands and corresponding stellar populations are beginning to be discovered.

arxiv-2507-02022.creator: Jerry J.-Y. Zhang (章俊龑), Nicolas Lodieu, Eduardo L. Martín
arxiv-2507-02022.description: Abstract We present deep K s K_{s} -band imaging of the extreme T subdwarf CWISE J221706.28 − - 145437.6. Using the new photometry, we construct its spectral energy distribution and find this object exhibits exceptionally strong collision-induced absorption in the H H and K K band. The comparison with the nearest benchmark extreme T subdwarf WISEA J181006.18 − - 101000.

arxiv-2507-11071.title: LogTinyLLM: Tiny Large Language Models Based Contextual Log Anomaly Detection
arxiv-2507-11071.creator: Isaiah Thompson Ocansey, Ritwik Bhattacharya, Tanmay Sen
arxiv-2507-11071.description: Abstract Log anomaly detection using traditional rule based or deep learning based methods is often challenging due to the large volumne and highly complex nature of log sequence. So effective way of detection of anomalous seqeunce of logs is crucial for system maintenance and development.

arxiv-2507-15992.title: Point counts, automorphisms, and gonalities of Shimura curves
arxiv-2507-15992.creator: Pietro Mercuri, Oana Padurariu, Frederick Saia, Claudio Stirpe
arxiv-2507-15992.description: Abstract . We implement an algorithm to compute the number of points over finite fields for the Shimura curves X 0 D ​ ( N ) X_{0}^{D}(N) and their Atkin–Lehner quotients. Our computations result in many examples of curves which attain the largest known point counts among curves of specified genus over a finite field of given cardinality.

arxiv-2512-03399.title: Full-Stack Alignment: Co‑Aligning AI and Institutions with Thick Models of Value
arxiv-2512-03399.creator: Joe Edelman, Tan Zhi-Xuan, Ryan Lowe, Oliver Klingefjord, Vincent Wang-Maścianica, Matija Franklin, Ryan Othniel Kearns, Ellie Hain, Atrisha Sarkar, Michiel Bakker, Fazl Barez, David Duvenaud, Jakob FoersterIason Gabriel, Joseph Gubbels, Bryce Goodman, Andreas Haupt, Jobst Heitzig, Julian Jara-Ettin
arxiv-2512-03399.description: Abstract Beneficial societal outcomes cannot be guaranteed by aligning individual AI systems with the intentions of their operators or users. Even an AI system that is perfectly aligned to the intentions of its operating organization can lead to bad outcomes if the goals of that organization are misaligned with those of other institutions and individuals.

pmc-10518961.title: Factors associated with overweight/obesity of children aged 6–12 years in Indonesia
pmc-10518961.creator: Sofi Oktaviani, Mayumi Mizutani, Ritsuko Nishide, Susumu Tanimura
pmc-10518961.description: BackgroundGlobally, the prevalence of childhood obesity has increased considerably, including in Indonesia. Obesity results from multifactorial interactions at the personal, familial, and environmental levels. However, little is known about the factors associated with overweight/obesity among children in Indonesia. This study is intended to identify personal, familial, and environmental factors associated with overweight/obesity in children aged 6–12 years in Indonesia.

pmc-10519953.title: Strain-induced degradation and recovery of flexible NbOx-based threshold switching device
pmc-10519953.creator: Jia Min Ang, Putu Andhita Dananjaya, Calvin Ching Ian Ang, Gerard Joseph Lim, Wen Siang Lew
pmc-10519953.description: We investigate the functionality of NbOx-based selector devices on a flexible substrate. It was observed that the failure mechanism of cyclic tensile strain is from the disruption of atom arrangements, which essentially led to the crack formation of the film.

pmc-10635855.title: Comparison of the effects of intraoperative remifentanil and sufentanil infusion on postoperative pain management in robotic gynecological surgery: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-10635855.creator: Tae-Yun Sung, Young Seok Jee, Sung-Ae Cho, Inho Huh, Seok-Jin Lee, Choon-Kyu Cho
pmc-10635855.description: BackgroundRemifentanil and sufentanil are potent short-acting synthetic opioid analgesics. The administration of remifentanil has been associated with the incidence of opioid-induced hyperalgesia. Opioid-induced hyperalgesia may be alleviated when opioids, such as morphine, are switched to sufentanil. Therefore, this retrospective observational study aimed to compare the effects of remifentanil and sufentanil on postoperative pain in patients undergoing robotic gynecological surgery.

pmc-10730688.title: Modulating signalling lifetime to optimise a prototypical animal opsin for optogenetic applications
pmc-10730688.creator: Jessica Rodgers, Phillip Wright, Edward R. Ballister, Rebecca B. Hughes, Riccardo Storchi, Jonathan Wynne, Franck P. Martial, Robert J. Lucas
pmc-10730688.description: Animal opsins are light activated G-protein-coupled receptors, capable of optogenetic control of G-protein signalling for research or therapeutic applications. Animal opsins offer excellent photosensitivity, but their temporal resolution can be limited by long photoresponse duration when expressed outside their native cellular environment.

pmc-11394719.title: The Enhancement Origin of Antioxidant Property of Carboxylated Lignin Isolated from Herbaceous Biomass Using the Maleic Acid Hydrotropic Fractionation
pmc-11394719.creator: Chen Su, Xiu Wang, Yongjun Deng, Douyong Min, Guigan Fang, Chen Huang, Vipin Chandra Kalia
pmc-11394719.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Lignin is endowed with antioxidant activity due to its diverse chemical structure. It is necessary to explore the relationship between antioxidant activity and the chemical structure of the lignin to develop its high-value utilization. Herein, we employed maleic acid (MA) as a hydrotropic agent to preferably isolate the lignin from distinct herbaceous sources (wheat straw and switchgrass) under atmospheric pressure conditions.

pmc-11662182.title: The Triage and Diagnostic Accuracy of Frontier Large Language Models: Updated Comparison to Physician Performance
pmc-11662182.creator: Michael Joseph Sorich, Arduino Aleksander Mangoni, Stephen Bacchi, Bradley Douglas Menz, Ashley Mark Hopkins, Amaryllis Mavragani, Christopher Williams, Qiming Shi
pmc-11662182.description: rrent capabilities and progress. The triage (level/urgency of care to seek) and diagnostic accuracy of the GPT-3 model were recently compared with 5000 lay individuals using the internet and 21 practicing primary care physicians [4]. The triage ability of GPT-3 was significantly inferior to that of physicians, having similar accuracy to lay individuals.

pmc-13311790.title: Effect of modified atmosphere packaging on preservation property and microbial communities of golden pompano (Trachinotus ovatus) fillets during 0 °C storage
pmc-13311790.creator: Yisheng Huang, Zewei Zhang, Bin Zhang, Chang Liu, Yuzhong Zheng, Hui Zhu, Laihao Li, Wanling Lin
pmc-13311790.description: The effects of air packaging (AP) and modified atmosphere packaging 1 (MAP1) (50% CO₂/50% N₂), MAP2 (70% CO₂/30% N₂), and MAP3 (90% CO₂/10% N₂) on the preservation property of Golden Pompano Trachinotus ovatus stored at 0 °C were studied. Results demonstrated that MAP exhibited better preservation effects than AP.

pmc-13366833.title: Menstrual product preference and factors associated with use of freely-distributed reusable products among secondary students in Uganda: a longitudinal study
pmc-13366833.creator: Levicatus Mugenyi, Ronald Kyasanku, Robert Bakanoma, Denis Ndekezi, Kate Andrews Nelson, Katherine A Thomas, Stephen Lagony, Aggrey Tumuhimbise, Jackline Namara, Norah Kembabazi, Andrew Mpaji, Shamirah Nakalema, Clare Tanton, Mandikudza Tembo, Nambusi Kyegombe, Helen A Weiss, Belen Torondel-Lopez
pmc-13366833.description: IntroductionAccess to menstrual products is a key factor for improving menstrual health, but there is limited research on the facilitators and barriers to their uptake and use. We describe menstrual product use, and factors associated with use of freely-distributed reusable pads and menstrual cups among female students in Ugandan secondary schools.

pmc-13604728.title: A Rapid and Sensitive Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification Assay for the Detection of Mulberry Mosaic Dwarf-Associated Virus
pmc-13604728.creator: Shaoshuang Sun, Xueping Zhou, Xiuling Yang
pmc-13604728.description: Mulberry mosaic dwarf-associated virus (MMDaV), a member of the genus Mulcrilevirus in the family Geminiviridae, poses a serious threat to mulberry cultivation and growth in China. Early and accurate diagnosis is a prerequisite for the effective prevention and control of MMDaV-related disease. In this study, a loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP)-based detection method was established for the specific identification of MMDaV.
